item.title: Mike Florio calls out Dan Quinn’s ‘word salad’ attempt to spin Commanders’ viral 4th-down play
item.description: Kyle Terada-Imagn Images Mike Florio calls out Dan Quinn’s ‘word salad’ attempt to spin Commanders’ viral 4th-down play appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Washington Commanders are 1-4-1 on the season after suffering a 23-17 Week 6 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. There was a moment early in the second quarter that went viral, as it appeared head coach Dan Quinn was shocked after his team failed a fourth-and-two play, as it seemed as though Quinn was unaware that it was fourth down. His explanation for the incident led to NFL insider Mike Florio blasting him on Tuesday morning. The 56-year-old informed media members during his postgame press conference that he was fully aware that it was fourth down on that particular play. But every word after that came off as confusing to Florio, who called out Quinn in his latest piece for Pro Football Talk . “‘I definitely knew it was fourth down,’ Quinn said, before slipping into a word salad that was largely confusing and pivoted to him explaining that they planned to go for it on fourth down throughout the game because they expected it to be a higher-scoring contest,” Florio wrote. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The viral clip does not confirm whether or not Quinn was confused about what down it was early in the second quarter. However, many believe he asks if it was fourth down or not with lip-syncing. The veteran head coach’s body language also suggests he was a bit confused about what was going on. However, that’s completely up for interpretation. “Oh that was 4th down” Dan Quinn out here guessing what down it is pic.twitter.com/oeLJAo85mF — Pardon My Take (@PardonMyTake) October 20, 2026 Either way, things are just not going well for the Commanders to begin the season. Especially in the last two games, as Washington ended Week 5 with a 27-27 tie with the New York Giants after botching the final play and allowing the clock to run out before they could even spike the ball to give themselves a chance at winning the contest with a field goal. We’ll see if Dan Quinn and his Commanders can bounce back in their next matchup. Washington has a bye in Week 7 before returning in Week 8 for a “Sunday Night Football” matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles, assuming the NFL doesn’t flex that game. item.title: Detroit Lions expect to have Kerby Joseph at some point this season
item.description: Dan Campbell didn't put a timeline on it, but the Detroit Lions coach said he expects All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph to be back in the lineup at some point this year. "I'm not going to give you a timetable, but I’m pleased with where he’s at," Campbell said. "He’s in a good headspace right now, which is great because that’s hard. You’re coming off of this, you’re wanting to go and you’re working at it, and at some point it’s time for football. We all know that and recognize it, but we take it one day at a time." Joseph has not played in 373 days, since a loss to the Kansas City Chiefs last Oct. 12, because of a cartilage issue in his knee. He opened the season on the physically unable to perform list and has not practiced this season Joseph said in late July he was "optimistic" he'd back early in the season , but he missed a large chunk of training camp for personal reasons, which set back his rehab. Joseph has been in good spirits in the locker room and as an observer at practice, which is in stark contrast to the dispirited mood he was in late last season when he tried to return from his injury but could not deal with the pain. "He’s doing well," Campbell said. "I’ll leave it at that. Really is. He’s doing a good job." GOING STREAKING? Lions looking for first back-to-back wins in over a year The Lions , 3-2 and coming off their bye week, are expected to get starting safety Brian Branch back from the PUP list for this week's game against the Green Bay Packers. Branch returned to practice before the bye but has not been added to the 53-man roster yet. Campbell said he expects Branch to play Sunday, Oct. 25, though he may be on a snap count. Chuck Clark, who's started every game at safety this year, and rookie Keith Abney, who played extensively at free safety in the Lions' Week 5 win over the Arizona Cardinals, could share playing time at the second safety spot opposite Branch, Campbell said. "Here’s what great about getting BB back," Campbell said. "BB gives you the flexibility of, what do you want to do with anybody else? And because there’s things you’re going to want to do with BB high, let him play top down, and then there’s things you want him to play underneath. And that doesn’t require somebody else playing off of him necessarily. He’ll make it right. That’s the beauty of – that’s where he and Kerby, man, go a long way. You’ve got safeties that are versatile and can do a lot of different jobs." Dave Birkett covers the Lions for the Detroit Free Press. Contact him at dbirkett@freepress.com . item.title: 76ers’ Kentavious Caldwell-Pope knows all about Ring Nights getting ruined, and he just sent Knicks a warning
item.description: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images 76ers’ Kentavious Caldwell-Pope knows all about Ring Nights getting ruined, and he just sent Knicks a warning appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia 76ers are just hours away from kicking off their new season against the New York Knicks on the road. The 76ers enter this season with legit championship aspirations after adding LeBron James and Jaylen Brown to the mix this summer. Prior to the game, the Knicks will be hoisting their banner from last season’s NBA championship, and one person who knows a thing or two about having a ring night spoiled is 76ers offseason addition Kentavious Caldwell-Pope . “I’ve had a few ruin my nights. It’s not fun. … If it’s their ring night, they gotta take the first loss,” he said, per Kristian Winfield of the New York Daily News on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Indeed, KCP has won multiple championships in his career, including one with James on the Los Angeles Lakers during the 2020 season. While neither James nor Caldwell-Pope is the same level of player they were during that triumph, they are still both serviceable veterans who figure to play a sizable role in what the 76ers are trying to accomplish this year. The 76ers are viewed by many as one of the most fascinating basketball experiments in recent NBA history, with the team hoping that its raw talent and star power will be enough to drown out concerns about perimeter shooting, defense, and, perhaps most importantly, the availability of their key players. Meanwhile, the Knicks are returning most of the same core from a year ago, one that swept the 76ers out of the playoffs in the second round last year, which will surely be on the minds of the Philadelphia players who are still on the team from that embarrassment. In any case, tipoff is set for 7:00 pm ET on Tuesday. Related: 76ers’ Jaylen Brown reveals to Lil Baby he’s a big harp guy, because why not? item.title: Brown And James Join TGL Roster For 2027 Season
item.description: Marc Lebryk-Imagn Images The TGL golf league is adding fresh blood for its third season. Mark Schlabach of ESPN reported Tuesday that Blades Brown and Ben James are joining the circuit. They arrive alongside rookie Jackson Koivun to fill out the rosters for the 2027 campaign. This move signals a shift toward younger talent as the league looks to build long-term interest. Tiger Woods also returns to lead the Jupiter Links GC after missing the entire second regular season due to injury. Brown made headlines on Oct. 11 by becoming the youngest Korn Ferry Tour graduate to earn a PGA Tour card. He finished ninth in the standings to secure his spot. James, a former standout at Virginia, joins the defending champion Los Angeles GC. He was the top player in the PGA Tour University rankings and earned four-time All-American honors. These two additions bring a mix of youth and proven skill to the indoor arena. New Roster Rules Take Effect The league is changing how teams are built for the upcoming year. ESPN reported that TGL increased roster sizes to five golfers for season three. Despite the larger roster size, only three players will actually compete in any single match. This format allows teams to carry depth while keeping the on-screen action focused. Rufus Hack, the president of golf for TMRW Sports, explained the strategy behind the change. “Our teams are developing distinct identities that reflect their players’ personalities and competitive fire, the character of the cities they represent and the vision of their ownership groups,” Hack said in a statement. The goal is to make each team feel unique and tied to its home city. With Motor City Golf Club joining as a new franchise, the league now has seven teams total. The expansion adds more room for rivalries to grow. Star Power and Team Dynamics Each team now features a blend of veterans and rising stars. item.title: Travis Kelce & Colston Loveland Headline Week 7 Fantasy Football Must-Bench Tight Ends
item.description: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce (87) reacts after a play during the second quarter against the Los Angeles Chargers at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Week 7 of the NFL season is here, and it's time to get your fantasy football team into playoff position or make a push back into the hunt. The tight end position can be especially difficult to navigate if you don't have one of the top five or six options, with weekly matchups often playing a major role in who you should start. Here are the tight ends you should consider fading in Week 7, along with better options to target. Travis Kelce @ Seattle Seahawks Sitting Travis Kelce? There may not have been a single week in the past decade when that idea made much sense. Times have changed, though, and so has the Kansas City offense. The Chiefs are no longer the high-flying, pass-heavy attack built around Patrick Mahomes airing it out. These days, Mahomes looks more like a game manager, and the offense runs through Kenneth Walker III. Kelce simply isn't the focal point he once was. Outside of a big performance against the Colts in Week 2, Kelce has struggled to command consistent targets. He's averaging just four targets per game across his other four contests, turning those opportunities into only 11 receptions. That's a concerning trend heading into a matchup with the Seahawks, who have been the league's toughest defense against tight ends, allowing just 25.5 receiving yards per game to the position. And this isn't a case of Seattle benefiting from weak competition; they've already faced Trey McBride and George Kittle. Kelce still has name recognition and touchdown upside, but his margin for error is shrinking. If he doesn't find the end zone, this could be a disappointing week for fantasy managers-and there may be better options available. item.title: Ronaldo let Man Utd down says Ten Hag
item.description: Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag speaking to Cristiano Ronaldo (Adrian DENNIS) Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has accused Cristiano Ronaldo of letting the team down during his time in charge. Portugal star Ronaldo was in his second spell at United when Ten Hag was hired in 2022. Ten Hag's relationship with Ronaldo quickly became tense and the striker refused to come on as a substitute in a win over Tottenham in the October 2022. Ronaldo was dropped for a subsequent match against Chelsea, prompting him to give an explosive television interview in which he said he felt betrayed by United and did not respect Ten Hag. The former Real Madrid forward's contract at United was mutually terminated the following month. "He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him," Ten Hag said in an interview with The Athletic. "Obviously, he's one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision and keep the players I admire in." Ten Hag said Ronaldo pulled out of training sessions and did not complete the full run that players were set after they were beaten 4-0 by Brentford early in his reign. "I confronted him with this. Many times I say, 'Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can't bring yourself in the box, you can't score'. He was not capable to do this," Ten Hag said. "It's the wrong idea to put this to me that I expected him to do the pressing, that he's exhausted. But he couldn't. "He ran neither in possession nor out of possession. The reason was because he didn't prepare himself." Ten Hag also claimed promises made by United's owners went unfulfilled before he was sacked in 2024, shortly after signing a new contract. Although United won the FA Cup just months earlier with a surprise final victory against Manchester City, Ten Hag was axed with the team languishing in 14th place in the Premier League. The Dutchman blamed the United hierarchy of some of his problems, saying he was left humiliated when Scotland midfielder Scott McTominay was sold to Napoli without his consent. Ten Hag also said he wanted to sign Harry Kane, Declan Rice and Frenkie de Jong during his spell at United. "They promised me loyalty, they promised me backing, they promised communication, that we get aligned. We spoke about the issues. But the promises, they didn't keep," he said. "I said, 'No selling Scott McTominay'. And in the end they sold him. I got, of course, very embarrassed and disappointed." smg/dmc

item.title: Jim Nantz lists himself as ‘questionable’ after Peanut Punch wrist injury, expects to be ‘a go’ for Bengals-Ravens
item.description: Credit: NFL on CBS Jim Nantz is going to play through it. According to Jimmy Traina, who said on his Traina Thoughts podcast that he texted Nantz asking for an on-the-record comment on his hand, the CBS play-by-play voice provided an injury update as a nervous nation sits on its hands waiting to learn whether he’ll be calling Sunday’s game in a cast. “Jimmy, I’ll probably be listed as questionable Wednesday when the first injury report comes out. Jim Rikhoff suggested they will work me out before the game Sunday in Baltimore, but I expect to be a go.” The injury happened during CBS’s broadcast of Sunday’s Bills-Raiders game, when Watt was explaining that ball carriers have started locking the wrist of their ball-carrying hand to protect against the “ Peanut Punch ,” a move popularized by Charles “Peanut” Tillman to force a fumble by punching the ball out of the carrier’s hands. To prove the technique works, Watt had the 67-year-old Nantz stand up and punch the football as hard as he could. Jim Nantz trying to “Peanut Punch” a football out of J.J. Watt’s hands is incredible live television. https://t.co/4X3Xq31JS0 — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) October 18, 2026 Nantz needed Watt to confirm twice that the invitation was real, and when Watt egged him on a second time, the 67-year-old rose from his chair, reared back, and unloaded a full-bodied haymaker on the football. Watt’s wrist-lock held without so much as a wobble, more than could be said for Nantz’s wrist, and CBS’s signature voice slumped back into his seat, cradling it, deadpanning that it was broken and returning from the commercial break nursing an ice pack. “Physical at times in that first half. Gonna be a few folks having to play hurt the last couple of quarters…” – Jim Nantz holding an ice pack https://t.co/oY2FpDm6y0 — NFL on CBS (@NFLonCBS) October 18, 2026 “Every announcer by week seven is broadcasting with some kind of bump or bruise,” Nantz told Traina. “I told J.J. they’re going to have to drag me out of the booth to stop me from talking.” Unless he suffers a setback, Nantz will be next to Watt in Baltimore on Sunday for Bengals-Ravens, and he’ll most likely leave the defensive demonstrations to the guy with three Defensive Player of the Year awards. item.title: Real Madrid midfielder’s situation has not changed despite signs of promise in international break
item.description: Real Madrid midfielder’s situation has not changed despite signs of promise in international break Zinedine Zidane’s decision to call up Eduardo Camavinga as part of his first national team list as the manager of Les Bleus came as a pleasant surprise for the Real Madrid player and club faithful. After all, the player has not been a regular for the men in white in a long time, and the manager’s decision to include him for the international break was seen as a chance for him to redeem himself. On international duty, he was handed minutes and importance by the manager and participated in 204 minutes across the four games, including a starting role in the wins against Belgium. The high did not continue As reported by MARCA now, Camavinga’s purple patch ended right where it began and has not arrived back in Madrid with the player. Camavinga had a positive international break. (Picture credit: Instagram/@camavinga) Despite his minutes of importance and decent performances for France, it has not moved him up Jose Mourinho’s pecking order at Real Madrid one bit. He continues to remain one of the manager’s last preferences in midfield. Before the international break, he was only a bench player for the club with only two starts in seven games. After the break, his misery has only continued as he has played just 25 minutes over the past three games. Federico Valverde, Aurelien Tchouameni, Arda Guler, Jude Bellingham and Bernardo Silva, all have played more minutes than Camavinga who is currently at one of the lowest points in his career. Time to reconsider? Camavinga refused to leave last summer. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Having emerged from the international break as one of Real Madrid’s bright sparks, there was much hope that Camavinga’s situation would change under Jose Mourinho. The fact that even his improved performances have not sufficed to make him a starter only adds weight to the argument that the player must leave the club, for there are not many optimistic signs that matters will change. At a point in time where Real Madrid are already struggling for creativity in midfield and looking to phase out higher-placed midfield names, the future does look bleak for the Frenchman who has fallen behind his teammates. He was reluctant to leave the club in June, but matters could change in the winter or the next summer transfer window, especially if Real Madrid indeed push for another new midfield signing.

item.title: Ryan Clark gives brutal Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen reality check to ‘MVP’ Brock Purdy
item.description: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images Ryan Clark is just not convinced about Brock Purdy’s case of being the best quarterback in the NFL with players like Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen still playing. The San Francisco 49ers QB has been in splendid form for his team, recording 1,460 passing yards at a 69.6% completion rate with 14 touchdowns to his name. He had another decent performance against the Washington Commanders, where he threw for 264 yards and had a touchdown in a 23-17 win for the 49ers. With him putting up big performances and the 49ers holding a 6-0 record, Brock Purdy has earned recognition in the MVP conversation. Ryan Clark not convinced about Brock Purdy being the best QB Purdy has been sensational ever since the 49ers took a chance and drafted him with the last pick in the 2022 NFL Draft. He has orchestrated multiple deep playoff runs and a Super Bowl appearance. However, to be named the best QB in the league, Purdy still has to outclass Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen. “As long as Patrick Mahomes & Josh Allen are alive it’ll be hard to call Brock Purdy the best quarterback in football… MVP Purdy right now,” Clark said on X. Interestingly, Purdy is yet to win any game played against Mahomes and Allen. He has been beaten by Mahomes in the Super Bowl and the regular season. Meanwhile Allen’s Bills dominated the 49ers in a 35-10 win in 2024. This season, Mahomes and Purdy are the only two QBs among the three who have an unbeaten record. Allen has only lost one game, but since then his team have looked brilliant and are firm favourites to win the AFC. Purdy definitely has elevated his game, but to Clark’s point, he is yet to prove that he is the best QB in the league. Allen and Mahomes both have the ability to shoulder their teams to deep playoff runs. Purdy has also managed to do that, despite injuries, but it will be interesting to see if he can sustain the brilliance. Currently, Purdy might be a favourite to win the MVP award, which will only help him add laurels to his resume. If he is to topple Allen and Mahomes, the 49ers QB will have to deliver some jaw-dropping, highlight-worthy performances, as that is what separates him from the other two superstars. item.description: CLEVELAND, OHIO - JANUARY 04: Nae'qwan Tomlin #35 of the Cleveland Cavaliers drives to the basket against Jaden Ivey #23 of the Detroit Pistons during the second half at Rocket Arena on January 04, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Cavaliers will be tipping off their season on Thursday against the Philadelphia 76ers without one of their rotation players. The team announced on Tuesday morning that Nae’Qwan Tomlin was “diagnosed with a lower back stress reaction following an evaluation by the Cavaliers medical team.” pic.twitter.com/OS0fXuZyH8 — Cleveland Cavaliers (@cavs) October 20, 2026 Per the Cavaliers’ statement, the team’s medical group identified this injury during an evaluation. Tomlin will be re-evaluated in three to four weeks. I wouldn’t assume that this timeline is definitive, especially with something like this that could vary in severity. It is also fair to note that, with the physical and athletic style of play Tomlin utilizes, this may not be as straightforward as other, more standard injuries. Without Tomlin, the Cavs are left with Mario Hezonja and Thomas Bryant as the two established backup bigs. That is far from an ideal group, as Hezonja is still an unknown at this point, while Bryant is a volatile option. This is definitely a missed opportunity for Tomlin to flash. Tomlin hasn’t been able to show much growth in areas of need for his game thus far, and the Cavaliers’ bench feels far from concrete at this point. The start to this season could have been one of the last chances Tomlin had to show he’s deserving of a steady role going forward. With at minimum a month to be missed to start the year, this injury is far from ideal both for Tomlin and the Cavaliers. Last season, Tomlin averaged 5.8 points and 2.9 assists in 64 outings and 15.2 minutes per game.

item.description: Pat McAfee celebrates alongside Steve Young after picking BYU to win against Notre Dame during the ESPN College Gameday show near Helaman Halls on the BYU campus in Provo on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026. | Lukas Katilius, Deseret News “College GameDay” certainly knew where it was Saturday. And while we’re likely to see fewer religious references emerge during this week’s show, it’s still the state of Utah and a football program that’s well-represented with Latter-day Saint fans, players and coaches, beginning with head coach Morgan Scalley. item.title: Harry Brook pinpoints exactly where England went wrong in Pakistan loss
item.description: Harry Brook admitted England ’s batters retreated into their shells against spin as their winter campaign began with a heavy 87-run defeat to Pakistan in the one-day international tri-series. Arafat Minhas arrived with Pakistan on 133 for five, but his 59 off 58 balls lifted them to 302 for nine before taking career-best figures of six for 40 to bowl England out. Openers Tom Banton and Ben Duckett shared 91, but England faltered against Arafat and holding off-spinner Saim Ayub, eventually falling for 215. Despite recent spin lessons from specialist mentor Kevin Pietersen on strike rotation, Brook conceded England lost momentum after Banton and Duckett laid the foundation. Arafat Minhas took six wickets (Getty) "At the halfway stage, we were pretty happy," England’s white-ball captain said. "I thought we kept them to just below par and we executed our plans exceptionally well and unfortunately we didn’t manage to get it quite right with the bat. "The story of the innings was not enough partnerships and losing wickets in clumps. We didn’t manage to put their bowlers under enough pressure to make them miss and that’s something we’ll talk about. "I probably could have hit the ball a little bit harder, but I think that was throughout. "We’ve been speaking a lot about rotation of strike against spin through the middle overs but we could still be putting bowlers under pressure and hit boundaries as well." Playing his fifth ODI, Arafat saw Banton pick out midwicket for 57 before bowling Brook with a turning delivery. He removed England's lower order and added a direct hit run-out, securing Pakistan's second win after beating Sri Lanka. Brook said: "He’s a nice bowler, he bowled very well. I thought they fielded exceptionally well. We’ve all seen videos of him but obviously we haven’t played against him much – but he was the standout performer by a mile." Arafat picked up the crucial wicket of Tom Banton, who was England's top scorer (Getty) England, facing Sri Lanka on Thursday, won all three ODI series this year after losing six of seven previously. With next year's World Cup in southern Africa approaching, Brook welcomed the tough test. "Definitely, and we’re definitely that side as well," Brook added. "We won’t go down without a fight and we’ll always be there or thereabouts. "It feels like that’s the most convincing loss we’ve had since last year sometime. It’s a good sign in one way but we’ve got tonight and tomorrow to talk about it and get ready for Sri Lanka on Thursday."

The Philadelphia Eagles have dominated the headlines in the NFL for all of the wrong reasons lately, as it was revealed that Jalen Hurts not only has a blood clot problem, but it has spread to his lungs, likely forcing him to miss the rest of the season. But it's worse than that, as it was revealed he played through Week 5 against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London with a blood clot. He played on little to no sleep in this game, and the Eagles' decision to let him play was a very controversial decision. However, according to Jonathan Jones of The Athletic , the Eagles will not face any punishment from the NFL for Hurts playing in Week 5. Despite fan outrage and questions from the media, the NFL determined the Eagles didn't commit any wrongdoing. NFL reportedly won't punish Eagles for Jalen Hurts blood clot situation "The NFL has concluded that the process surrounding Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts being cleared to play in Week 5 with a superficial blood clot 'was handled appropriately,' a league source tells The Athletic," Jones reports. That same source told Jones and The Athletic that the NFL will "not issue any punishment to the Eagles for its handling of the medical process, or for Hurts not being given an injury designation ahead of the game." A day after Nick Sirianni was grilled by reporters about Hurts' health and the decision to play him through blood clots and minimal sleep, the NFL has determined the Eagles did no wrong. MORE : Giants' QB plans get complicated after Jameis Winston collapse, J.J. McCarthy surge It doesn't change the fact that playing Hurts in such a situation is a risky decision they really shouldn't have taken. Tanner McKee and Cole Payton could've manned the QB position for that one week in London. Instead, Hurts played and flew back home before it was revealed to be a more serious blood clot issue than it initially appeared to be. Hurts is now out for the season with blood clots discovered in his lungs, requiring blood thinners to treat him. While he can make a full recovery, it's not likely to happen until the 2026 season is well over. Despite the outcry over the Eagles' decision to play him through such a scary injury, the NFL isn't punishing the Eagles. For now, it appears this situation has concluded, with the hope being that Hurts' recovery goes well and he can come back for the 2027 season. item.title: Fabregas rejects Man Utd ‘crisis’ talk ahead of Champions League meeting
item.description: Fabregas rejects Man Utd ‘crisis’ talk ahead of Champions League meeting Cesc Fabregas has rejected the claim that Manchester United are in “crisis” ahead of the clash between his Como side and the Premier League club on Wednesday. United have picked up just two wins this season, with one coming against Sabah FK in the first matchday of the Champions League. In the past week they have succumbed to a 2-0 loss at Atlético Madrid that was followed with a 1-1 draw against Leeds United at Elland Road on Sunday. He said: “I don’t believe in crises in football, you have a game every three days, it’s 11 against 11, and you’ve got to give your best. “A crisis is invented by you journalists, but we are professionals, we’ve wanted to compete since the day we were born. I don’t believe in any crisis.” Pressure on Michael Carrick has increased but Fabregas refused to answer if he would like the Manchester United job if it became available “out of respect for Carrick and an institution like United”. Como sit fifth in Serie A and have won one and lost one in the Champions League so far. They won their first ever game in the competition against RB Leipzig 4-1 but were beaten 3-2 by Feyenoord last week. Looking ahead to Wednesday’s game, Fabregas said: “It is another historic day for the club, the fans and the city. “We’ve got to play with focus and ambition. This is Manchester United we are up against, so let’s enjoy it, play our game and try to win. It’s an incredible group of players, so we must be humble and realise there is much to learn. We’ll see how it goes but we respect our opponents. “There are different ways of attacking, we try to study their weaknesses but also don’t forget what we do best. They have a specific system and principles, but football is ultimately about the players. We tend to forget that, as directors and coaching staff.” Como’s league form has suffered with the more strenuous schedule that comes with involvement in Europe’s elite competition. Fabregas said: “Many players have never done this before, but we’ve got to improve and play with ambition. “We cannot talk too much about history, because otherwise these players step onto the field with fear. A coach must give his players confidence. If we think we’re higher than we are, then it will be more difficult.”

item.title: Nobody calls a game better’: ESPN stars throw support behind Troy Aikman
item.description: Oct 21, 2021; Cleveland, Ohio, USA; NFL Half of Fame quarterback Troy Aikman before the game between the Cleveland Browns and the Denver Broncos at FirstEnergy Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Scott Galvin-USA TODAY Sports Troy Aikman has been a fixture on ESPN’s Monday Night Football the last several years, but now the Hall of Fame quarterback’s future with the network is in doubt. Joe Buck, Aikman’s longtime broadcast partner, has reupped with the Worldwide Leader, but Aikman is still working on the final year of his original deal. The situation has caused “tension” between the two colleagues, which reportedly boiled over in the booth before last Monday’s game. With Aikman leaving ESPN now a real possibility, some of the network’s biggest names are rallying in support of the Dallas Cowboys legend. Stephen A., Michael Wilbon speak up Michael Wilbon, co-host of Pardon the Interruption , ESPN’s longest-running show, sent a not-so-subtle message about Aikman to company higher-ups during a recent episode. “You know who calls a game better than Troy Aikman, knuckleheads? Nobody calls a game better than Troy Aikman!” Wilbon said, via the New York Post . On Monday, Stephen A. Smith, who is arguably ESPN’s biggest star, said he “sincerely hopes” Aikman returns to the Worldwide Leader. “They are the A-team,” Smith said on his SiriusXM show, via Awful Announcing . “Joe Buck, it don’t get no better, play-by-play. Excuse the double negative. It’s just the truth. And I feel the exact same way about Troy Aikman, who I love, who I’ve loved for years. That’s their business, that’s ESPN’s business, that’s ABC’s business, and all of that. I know they’ll be calling the Super Bowl this year. “Troy Aikman is a three-time Super Bowl champion, an elite football mind whose credentials and resume is as impeccable as they come, and it speaks for itself. I sincerely hope that we don’t lose him as a person that’s employed by ESPN, but if we do lose him, I want to wish him all the happiness in the world if he decides to go elsewhere. Because football must have Troy Aikman’s voice in it, he’s that special of a guy and a football mind, and I sincerely hope that we keep him.” Aikman prepared for an exit Back in September, Aikman said he thought his contract status would have been solved already and “when it might get done, if it gets done, is anyone’s guess.” More recently, the 59-year-old has been less than enthusiastic about the possibility of ESPN wanting him back. “It just seems to be where they’re going — that they’re gonna go in a different direction because there’s been no talks, no contract negotiations,” Aikman told Jimmy Traina last week. item.title: UConn women's basketball team is No. 2 in the preseason AP Top 25 poll
item.description: Geno Auriemma, head coach of the UConn Huskies, looks on during the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame women's college basketball exhibition game between the Syracuse Orange and the UConn Huskies at Mohegan Sun Arena in Uncasville, United States, on October 12, 2026. (Photo by Erica Denhoff/NurPhoto via Getty Images) (NurPhoto/NurPhoto via Getty Images) The UConn women's basketball team will begin the 2026-27 season ranked second in the country. The preseason Associated Press Top 25 poll was unveiled Tuesday afternoon and South Carolina sits at No. 1. The Huskies, who lost to South Carolina in the Final Four last year, are second ahead of USC, Duke and Michigan. Rounding out the Top 10: Texas, Louisville, Vanderbilt, LSU and Iowa. The Huskies beat Texas in a preseason game Monday night. South Carolina received 23 of 31 first-place votes. UConn received six first-place votes, USC two. UConn began last season No. 1 after winning the NCAA title in 2025. The Huskies maintained the top spot all season before losing the Final Four. South Carolina beat UConn handily in the national semifinal, but lost 79-51 to UCLA in the title game. The Bruins finished atop the AP poll after its title run, but begin this season at No. 11. Geno Auriemma's Huskies were first ranked in the Top 25 in the 1989-90 season. UConn first reached No. 1 in January 1995. UConn has also been in the Top 10 of every preseason poll since 1994. UConn and South Carolina will meet at Mohegan Sun Arena on Nov. 24. Other Top 25 opponents on UConn's schedule: Michigan, Iowa, Louisville, Ohio State, Duke, Maryland, Notre Dame, and LSU. item.title: 49ers’ Deebo Samuel missed Commanders game with injury, but that didn’t stop him from a viral e-date appearance
item.description: David Gonzales-Imagn Images. 49ers’ Deebo Samuel missed Commanders game with injury, but that didn’t stop him from a viral e-date appearance appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . While he missed the San Francisco 49ers ’ win against the Washington Commanders, his former team, injured wide receiver Deebo Samuel still made time for e-dating. He hosted an e-dating stream on TikTok (via the New York Post), acting as a wingman for prospective couples as they spoke to each other. Samuel didn’t take part in the e-dating, as he is in a relationship with Mahogany Jones. His role was purely as a matchmaker for the participants. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Niners continued their undefeated streak by beating the Commanders on Monday Night Football. It’s all fun and games now, but the matchmaker’s team may play on Valentine’s Day in the Super Bowl if they continue on their current path. 49ers WR Deebo Samuel ’s stats before injury Credit: David Gonzales-Imagn Images While he missed the 49ers’ last game, he has been a big part of the offense in his reunion with the team (he spent a year with the Commanders before returning to the Niners in 2026). He has caught 16 passes for 206 yards and three touchdowns. Samuel notably logged 80 yards and a touchdown without a reception during the team’s Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals. He has also rushed for 78 yards on nine carries. During his first stint with the 49ers, Samuel made it to one Pro Bowl team and one First-team All-Pro, both in 2021. That year, he caught a career-high 77 passes for 1,405 yards and six touchdowns. He remained with the team through the 2024 season. With the Commanders, he played in 16 games and logged 72 catches for 727 yards and five touchdowns. The 49ers are rolling six weeks into the season. They are one of the NFL’s three undefeated teams and the only one to reach six wins (the Kansas City Chiefs and the Minnesota Vikings only have five wins). item.title: Insider reveals where Aaron Boone, Brian Cashman have ‘failed’ Yankees
item.description: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Insider reveals where Aaron Boone, Brian Cashman have ‘failed’ Yankees appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Yankees are expected to keep manager Aaron Boone despite falling short of the World Series once again in 2026. The expectation is that general manager Brian Cashman will also be back. MLB insiders Joel Sherman and Jon Heyman recently addressed the situation during an episode of The Show with Joel Sherman & Jon Heyman. “You do have to think about what kind of people you put on the roster. Are those the guys you want taking at-bats, fielding the ball, making big decisions in the postseason? I think it’s a place where the Yankees have failed,” Sherman said. “Which means where Brian Cashman has failed and his group, by not having a greater appreciation of that. And I also think it’s a place where Aaron Boone has failed by not getting the full attention of some of these players, if that is actually possible.” The Yankees have had the talent to compete. Sherman seems to think the way Cashman and Boone have approached some of the elements of strategy and the roster has been an issue, though. So, how can these concerns be fixed? Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I think they need to put, for better terms, a bad cop, an enforcer, somebody next to him in the bench coach role,” Sherman added. “Who is more somebody who cares about the brand and cares about good baseball, and is willing to do what Boone hasn’t been willing to do which is call out publicly to some degree guys who are not playing the right way. Who are not valuing the scoreboard. Who are doing their thing over what’s good for the group.” The Yankees will attempt to bounce back next season as they look to win their first World Series since 2009. item.title: 'Not a very nice question' - Fabregas furiously dismisses disrespectful rumours about replacing Carrick at Manchester United
item.description: ACF Fiorentina v Como 1907 - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Como manager Cesc Fabregas has fiercely rejected speculation suggesting he is being lined up to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United. Ahead of a crucial Champions League clash between the two sides on Wednesday, the Spaniard refused to entertain questions about taking the Old Trafford dugout, labelling the line of enquiry as highly disrespectful to his former Premier League rival. A clash of Champions League ambitions Fabregas was questioned during his pre-match news conference about potentially taking over from Carrick , who is currently enduring a difficult run of six games without a victory. Manchester United travel to Italy to face Como in the Champions League on Wednesday, having secured just two wins all season. However, Fabregas was quick to shut down the narrative, defending Carrick and praising the work he has done. The Como boss made it clear he would not be drawn into discussing a role that is currently occupied by someone he deeply respects. Hitting back at the media Hitting back at the media When pressed on the possibility of managing Manchester United, Fabregas firmly defended Carrick. "I won't answer that question because I think that's not a very nice question," Fabregas stated on Tuesday. "I don't think that shows enough respect to a great footballer and manager like Michael Carrick at the helm of a wonderful Manchester United side." Fabregas and Carrick battled numerous times during their playing careers, and the Como manager evidently feels a strong sense of solidarity with his counterpart as Manchester United prepare for their demanding visit to the Sinigaglia. Respecting the Old Trafford legacy Despite their poor form, Fabregas remains cautious about underestimating Manchester United and their historical pedigree. "Manchester United is a historical club I know very, very well," said Fabregas. "We have so much respect for who they are, for what they do, because they have incredible players." Fabregas also highlighted his connection to the Manchester United coaching staff, noting his familiarity with Steve Holland from their time together at Chelsea. Como enter the fixture in excellent form, sitting fifth in the Serie A table following a 3-1 victory over Fiorentina at the weekend. What to expect on Wednesday? What to expect on Wednesday? While the managerial speculation will undoubtedly continue to swirl around Manchester United, Fabregas remains completely focused on Como and their upcoming Champions League test. A positive result on Wednesday would further cement his growing reputation as an elite coach, while Carrick desperately needs a victory to relieve the mounting pressure.

item.title: Detroit Lions still expect Kerby Joseph to play this year
item.description: Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph (31) practices during OTAs at Detroit Lions headquarters and training facility in Allen Park on Thursday, May 30, 2024. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co While the Detroit Lions are getting one of their Pro Bowl safeties back this week in Brian Branch , the return of the other—Kerby Joseph—remains a bit of a mystery. Joseph has now been sidelined for over a year with a knee injury that has been described as inoperable and chronic. Joseph’s timeline has seemingly been pushed back at every turn, but Lions coach Dan Campbell may have finally offered a light at the end of the tunnel. When asked if he expects Joseph to play this season, Campbell answered simply: “I do.” Campbell didn’t provide a timeline for Joseph’s return, but did say they are very encouraged with where things currently stand with his progress. “He’s doing well. I’ll leave it at that. He really is,” Campbell said. “He’s doing a good job. I’m not going to give you a timetable, but I’ve been pleased with where he’s at. He’s in a good headspace right now, which is great, because that’s hard. You’re coming off this, you’re wanting to go, and you’re working at it, and at some point, it’s time for football. We all know that and recognize it, but we’ll take it one day at a time.” A few weeks ago, Branch also offered some hope for Branch’s return. “Kerb’s my dawg. We’ve been—we ain’t quitting, man,” Branch said two weeks ago. “Injured, we’ve been in this thing together for, what, 10 months, man? It’s been a long road. We’ve been fighting every day. He gonna be alright. He gonna be back. We’re gonna be back.” Joseph has been back in the building for a few weeks now after taking some time away for a personal issue. He has not spoken with the media since the very beginning of training camp, when he noted that he was “super optimistic” because of all the work he’s put in . We haven’t had a healthy version of both Branch and Joseph on the field really since the 2024 season. But it looks like the Lions are expected to see it happen again at some point before the season is through.

item.description: European governing body gives two-week deadline Letter addresses other issues including Balogun affair Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body . A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months. These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights, the Folarin Balogun affair , the peace prize and relations with Donald Trump and the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election. Uefa’s document also makes a number of allegations about potential conflicts of interests at Fifa, as well as repeating calls for a “genuinely independent” governance review. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
